text:
This is a division game between teams a point apart, fourth and fifth in the Pacific, and both have been outchanced: 45% of the expected goals at five on five each (expected goals are the quality of chances). The difference is games in hand. San Jose has played 24, Seattle 19, which is why our playoff race has the Kraken at 30% and the Sharks at 6% despite the Sharks sitting ahead.

San Jose's story is the kids. Macklin Celebrini, Ivar Stenberg and Will Smith have become a line people talk about, and Smith's three points against Nashville drew "best game of his career" coverage from San Jose Hockey Now. Stenberg has stepped into Igor Chernyshov's spot, up to almost 20 minutes a night, and Michael Misa is up to nearly 18. Kiefer Sherwood is out until about Dec 1 and was seen in a sling. Mason Marchment, with a four-game point streak, faces the team that traded him. Yaroslav Askarov has 3.8 goals saved above expected after a rough first year in teal.

Seattle is living a little above its means. The Kraken are minus 5 in goals on minus 11.9 expected, and finishing (8.1 goals more than their chances usually produce) explains it. Berkly Catton is the face of that: a hat trick against Vancouver Thursday and 11 points in ten, partly real but mostly shooting luck by our measure. Still, he's 19 games into his second season and looking like a top-six player. Jared McCann is out until January, so Kaapo Kakko has taken his spot beside Matty Beniers and Mackie Samoskevich, a line Alison Lukan said "cooked" against Vancouver, and Beniers has moved onto the top power play. Joey Daccord was pulled in back-to-back games recently, and Philipp Grubauer is our projected starter.

The Sharks take 4.6 penalties a game, the clearest edge Seattle has in a matchup that otherwise looks very even on chances.
headline: Two young Pacific teams, one point apart
